name: Dockerfile Security
description: Enforces Dockerfile security patterns including non-root users, minimal base images, and multi-stage builds.
content:
# Dockerfile Security Rules

- Never run containers as root — add `USER nonroot` or `USER 1001` after installing dependencies
- Use minimal base images — `alpine`, `distroless`, or `-slim` variants to reduce attack surface
- Use multi-stage builds — build in a full image, copy only artifacts to a minimal runtime image
- Pin base image versions with SHA digests — `FROM node:20-alpine@sha256:abc123` not just `FROM node:latest`
- Don't store secrets in images — use build-time secrets (`--mount=type=secret`) or runtime environment variables
- Combine RUN commands with `&&` to reduce layers — fewer layers means smaller images and less cached state
- Use `.dockerignore` to exclude `node_modules`, `.git`, `.env`, and test files from the build context
- Set `HEALTHCHECK` instructions — let orchestrators know when your container is actually ready
- Don't install unnecessary packages — no `curl`, `wget`, or `vim` in production images unless required
- Use `COPY` instead of `ADD` — `ADD` has implicit behaviors (URL fetching, tar extraction) that can be surprising
- Scan images for vulnerabilities with Trivy, Snyk, or Docker Scout before deploying
- Set filesystem to read-only where possible — `--read-only` flag prevents runtime file modifications
